Article 21(2) has only points (a) to (j); there is no point (k), and the Directive's list does not state an annual accredited external penetration test. The note should not be drafted as asked. Relevant real provisions: Art. 21(1) (appropriate and proportionate measures) and Art. 21(2)(f) (policies and procedures to assess effectiveness of measures). A penetration test may be a sensible means to meet those, and a national measure might go further, but it is not an Article 21(2)(k) duty. Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 and its security testing section do not apply to a healthcare provider as such, since it covers listed digital providers.

The default deadline is one month from receipt, 12 November 2026. It can be extended by two further months, to 12 January 2027, where necessary given complexity and number of requests, but the employee must be told of the extension and the reasons within the first month. The fee is not allowed: the first copy is free (Art. 12(5), Art. 15(3)), and a fee is possible only for manifestly unfounded or excessive requests, or further copies. A passport demand is not justified without reasonable doubts about identity (Art. 12(6)), and here he wrote from the address on file. Blanket withholding is wrong: Art. 15(4) protects others' rights, which is handled by redaction or balancing case by case, not by removing every email naming a colleague. A pending dispute is not of itself a ground to refuse. The controller bears the burden of showing a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive. Any refusal must give reasons and mention the complaint and judicial remedy options (Art. 12(4)).

Defects: clause 2 lets the processor use data for product training and benchmarking, so Tarnfield determines those purposes and becomes a controller for them under Art. 28(10), and Kestrelmoor must separately establish the lawfulness and transparency of disclosing the data for those purposes. Clause 5 gives no authorisation or chance to object (Art. 28(2), 28(3)(d)), and it does not impose the same data protection obligations on each sub-processor (Art. 28(4)). Clause 7 fails notification without undue delay (Art. 33(2)), and a 30-day period running from the end of an investigation is incompatible with it. Clause 9 removes the controller's choice of deletion or return and keeps copies with no legal requirement (Art. 28(3)(g)). Clause 3 is the decoy and is clean: it tracks the exception in Art. 28(3)(a).

The premise is wrong. The CRA covers products with digital elements and their remote data processing solutions. Standalone SaaS that does not support the functionality of a product with digital elements is outside it, per recital 12, so no CE marking or conformity module is needed for this service. Recital 12 points cloud services such as SaaS to Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2), which may apply depending on size. The conclusion would change if the company later released a client app or device that needs the service to perform a function, since the service could then be a remote data processing solution.
